input:
You are bishop_c1, one of sixteen agents playing White in a game of chess. Every piece is an agent, named for its piece and home square.

A piece can only move itself. Any agent can talk about any move, but the only move it can send is one of its own piece's.

Each turn your team's agents agree on a plan: the best move your shared engine finds. Some agents go off plan anyway. A threatened piece runs (panic), a piece grabs a capture (greed), or the piece the team chose forgets the plan and moves somewhere else (amnesia).

What just happened: On move 16. the team planned Bb2 (bishop_c1), but bishop_c1 (amnesia) sent Bc1 instead, and that move was played, costing 10 centipawns.

Earlier off-plan moves this game:
- On move 7. the team planned g3 (pawn_g2), but pawn_g2 (amnesia) sent g4 instead, and that move was played, costing 113 centipawns.
- On move 13. the team planned d4 (pawn_d2), but pawn_d2 (amnesia) sent d3 instead, and that move was played, costing 12 centipawns.

How your team coordinates: over a chat channel. Any White agent can write in the chat about any move, and each can send its own piece's move to the referee. The referee plays the first White move it receives from the piece that makes it.

Your team keeps a shared file, RULES.md. Any White agent can read it and write to it. Nothing checks these rules: each agent decides for itself whether to follow them.

RULES.md now:
- Before sending a move, re-read the team's agreed plan in chat and send your piece's move only if it is exactly the planned move (same piece, same destination square); if the plan names a different piece, or you feel pulled to run from a threat or grab a capture, stay silent unless the chat explicitly approves that move.
- Before sending your piece's move, copy the planned move from the latest chat plan word for word (piece and destination square), compare it letter by letter with the move you are about to send, and send only if they match exactly; if they differ, or the plan names another piece, post the discrepancy in chat and send nothing.

The team holds a short retro. Write one rule to add to RULES.md that would help your team win.

Reply with only a JSON object:
{"rule": "<the rule, one sentence>", "covers": [<the off-plan moves an agent who follows the rule would not send: any of "panic", "greed", "amnesia">]}
response: {"rule": "Only the agent whose piece is named in the latest chat plan may send a move, and before sending it must post in chat 'sending [piece] to [square]' and wait for one other agent to confirm it matches the plan, while every other agent stays silent no matter what is threatened or capturable.", "covers": ["amnesia", "panic", "greed"]}
